content: Sodium metabisulfite, also known as sodium pyrosulfite, is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Na₂S₂O₅. It is sometimes referred to as disodium metabisulfite. This compound is commonly used as a sterilizing agent and as an antioxidant or preservative. Uses Food Additive Sodium metabisulfite is widely used as a food additive, primarily as a preservative. It is often identified by the code E223. However, it can cause adverse reactions in some individuals, such as eczema, gastric irritation, and asthma. Due to these potential health effects, it is not recommended for consumption by children. It is commonly found in products like fruit juice concentrates and candy bars, such as Mounds. Sterilization and Cleaning Agent This compound is frequently used in homebrewing to sanitize equipment. It is also employed as a cleaning agent for potable water reverse osmosis membranes in desalination systems. Additionally, it is used to remove chloramine from drinking water after treatment. Stump Removal In products like Stump-Out, sodium metabisulfite is used in nearly pure form (98%) to degrade lignin in tree stumps. This process creates pores that facilitate fuel absorption and subsequent ignition. Packaging Sodium metabisulfite is available in powdered form. It is a primary ingredient in Campden tablets and some stump removal products. In its solid state, it ranges in color from white to slightly yellow. Chemical Properties When dissolved in water, sodium metabisulfite releases sulfur dioxide (SO₂), a gas with a pungent and unpleasant odor. This gas can cause respiratory difficulties in sensitive individuals. Due to these issues, the use of sodium metabisulfite has declined in favor of alternatives like hydrogen peroxide, which provides effective sterilization without the associated odor. However, the sulfur dioxide released by sodium metabisulfite makes the water a strong reducing agent. Alternatives In some applications, ascorbates (E300–E304) are used as alternatives to sodium metabisulfite. For flour improvement, calcium sulfate (E516) and ascorbic acid (E300) are considered safer substitutes.
